review.summary: This round has shown a continued lack of improvement in both factual correctness and clarity regarding the formation of yes/no questions in Swedish. critic_scores.rationale: The claim that yes/no questions in Swedish are formed by adding 'nej' (meaning 'no') to the end of a sentence is completely incorrect. In Swedish, yes/no questions are formed by inverting the subject and verb (verb-subject order), similar to other Germanic languages — for example, 'Du talar svenska' (You speak Swedish) becomes 'Talar du svenska?' (Do you speak Swedish?). The revision instructions explicitly flagged this error (FC-001) twice, yet the output is identical to the previous incorrect draft with no corrections made.
critic_scores.improvement_tip: Rewrite the explanation to correctly state that Swedish yes/no questions are formed through subject-verb inversion: move the finite verb to the first position before the subject, and add a question mark. Provide a clear example pair such as 'Han är trött.' → 'Är han trött?' to illustrate the rule.
